# PLAN — ISSUE-179: Check changelog fragment format at PR time

This adds a check-only mode to `internal/changelog` and `cmd/changelog` (`--check`). It parses every `changes/unreleased/*.md` fragment through the existing `fragment` parser without writing anything, and reports each malformed fragment by file name and reason. The check is wired into `make check` and runs as a repository-level Go test, so the existing CI `go test` step and the required `test` check both reject a PR that adds a malformed fragment. No protected policy files change (`allow_harness_changes: false`). The fragment format and the fold output stay the same.

## Dimensions (advisory; the WorkUnit sets none)

- Size: small (one new Go file, one new test file, roughly 15 changed lines across `cmd/changelog/main.go` and `Makefile`, one doc paragraph, one fragment).
- Uncertainty: low.
- Risk: low. `Fold` and `fragment` are not modified.

## What we know

- `Fold` is the only place fragments are parsed. It parses them only after a valid version is given and fragments exist (`internal/changelog/fold.go:21`, `:48-62`). It stops at the first bad fragment (`fold.go:57-60`), so it cannot report every malformed file.
- `fragment` (`fold.go:122`) holds the one-bullet rule. Its error text "each fragment holds exactly one bullet" is asserted by `TestFoldRejectsInvalidFragments` (`fold_test.go:145`) and `TestMakeChangelog` (`fold_test.go:219`). It must be reused as is.
- `Fold` lists entries with path-based `os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(root, ...))` (`fold.go:35`) even though it already holds a pinned `dir` from `r.Sub` (`fold.go:27`). The new check does not copy that. It lists entries from the pinned handle (`dir.OpenDirectory(".")`, `internal/safefs/root.go:136`) and reads each file with `dir.ReadFile` (`root.go:161`, regular files only, size-bounded, symlinks rejected).
- `r.Sub(..., false, 0)` returns an error matching `os.ErrNotExist` when the directory is missing. `Fold` already relies on this (`fold.go:28`).
- `cmd/changelog/main.go:11-14` accepts exactly one argument (VERSION). `versionToken` (`fold.go:16`) requires an alphanumeric first character, so `--check` can never be a valid version. No other code or test asserts the usage string (`grep -rn changelog --include=*.go internal cmd`).
- `Makefile:44` defines `check: lint race`, and `Makefile:54-58` defines `changelog`. The README (`README.md:81`) says `make check` runs the same checks as CI.
- `internal/testutil.WriteExecutable` (`internal/testutil/executable.go:12`) is the shared helper for writing executable test scripts without "text file busy". `TestMakeChangelog` uses it for a `go` wrapper that runs `"$3"` (`fold_test.go:239-241`). For `$(GO) run ./cmd/changelog --check`, `$3` is `--check`, so the same wrapper shape works.
- CI (`.github/workflows/swarm-validate.yml`, read-only) runs `go test -race -timeout 15m ./...`, and the approved required check runs `go test ./...`. A test in `internal/changelog` that checks `../..` therefore runs in existing CI, the same way `TestRepositoryUnreleasedEmpty` (`fold_test.go:338`) already does.
- The 7 current fragments (`changes/unreleased/160.md` … `281.md`) are each a single `- ` line (read with `cat`), so the new repository test passes on the current base.
- New files are absent at the approved base (checked with `ls`): `internal/changelog/check.go`, `internal/changelog/check_test.go`, `changes/unreleased/179.md`.

## What we're assuming

- Non-`.md` entries are ignored, matching `Fold`. A `.md` entry that is a directory, symlink, or FIFO is reported as malformed (the reason comes from safefs), not silently skipped. To check: the `TestCheck` table cases.
- Reading a FIFO through `dir.ReadFile` does not block, because safefs opens with `nonblock` and rejects non-regular files (`root.go:100-135`). `TestFoldRejectsSpecialFile` already shows this for `Fold`. To check: the FIFO case in `TestCheck`.

## Open questions

- The objective mentions "a required check in `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml` plus the scaffolded template". That file is protected and harness changes are not allowed. The acceptance criteria accept `make check` instead, and the operator said not to edit protected policy, so this plan uses `make check` plus the repository-level test. Adding the check to the policy and the scaffolded template is a **recommended follow-up WorkUnit** with `allow_harness_changes: true`.

## Design

### New: `internal/changelog/check.go`

```go
// Check parses every unreleased fragment without writing and reports each
// malformed one. A missing or empty fragment directory passes.
func Check(root string) error
```

1. Call `safefs.Open(root)`. Call `r.Sub("changes/unreleased", false, 0)`. If the error is `os.ErrNotExist`, return nil. Return any other error.
2. Call `dir.OpenDirectory(".")`, then `(*os.File).ReadDir(-1)` on that pinned descriptor. Collect names ending in `.md` and sort them, as `Fold` does.
3. For each name, call `dir.ReadFile(name, 4<<20)` and then `fragment(string(data))`. Wrap each failure as `fmt.Errorf("fragment %s: %w", name, err)` (same wording as `Fold`) and append it. Keep going after a failure.
4. Return `errors.Join(problems...)`. That is nil when there are no problems, and one line per malformed fragment otherwise, in filename order.

Nothing is created, written, renamed, or removed. Only the read-only safefs calls `Open`, `Sub(create=false)`, `OpenDirectory`, and `ReadFile` are used.

### Modified: `cmd/changelog/main.go`

- Update the package doc: the command folds release fragments, or checks them with `--check`.
- If `len(os.Args) == 2 && os.Args[1] == "--check"`, run `changelog.Check(".")`. If it returns an error, print it to stderr and exit 1. Otherwise exit 0.
- Change the usage text to `usage: changelog VERSION | changelog --check`. The fold path stays the same.

### Modified: `Makefile`

- Add a `changelog-check` target documented with a `##` comment, in the existing `.PHONY: changelog` block: `$(GO) run ./cmd/changelog --check`.
- `check: lint race changelog-check`. Update the `## check:` comment to mention fragments.

### Modified: `docs/developer.md` (Changelog fragments section, around line 611)

- Add one sentence: `make check` (or `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`) validates every fragment without writing and names each malformed file.

### New: `changes/unreleased/179.md`

- `- Check changelog fragment format in make check and CI tests so malformed fragments fail on the PR that adds them.`

## Implementation sequence

1. Add `check.go` with `Check`.
2. Add `check_test.go` (see TEST_PLAN). Do not change the existing `fold_test.go` tests.
3. Update `cmd/changelog/main.go`.
4. Update the `Makefile`.
5. Update the docs paragraph and add `changes/unreleased/179.md`.
6. Run `gofmt -s -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `make check`.

## HANDOFF

**Entry points and symbols**
- `internal/changelog/fold.go:122` `fragment`: reuse, do not modify.
- `internal/changelog/fold.go:21` `Fold`: do not modify (the fold output must stay the same).
- `internal/safefs/root.go:92` `Sub`, `:136` `OpenDirectory`, `:161` `ReadFile`: read-only APIs for the check.
- `cmd/changelog/main.go:10-19` `main`: add the `--check` branch.
- `Makefile:44` `check`, `Makefile:54-58` `changelog` block: add `changelog-check`.

**Existing tests and fixtures to reuse**
- `fold_test.go` helpers `put`, `read`, `fixture` (same package, usable from `check_test.go`).
- `TestMakeChangelog` (`fold_test.go:219`) wrapper pattern with `testutil.WriteExecutable`. The new make test copies this pattern and uses the shared helper. Do not add a new script writer.
- `TestRepositoryUnreleasedEmpty` (`fold_test.go:338`): the model for the repository-level test.

**Focused verification**
```bash
go test -race -run 'TestCheck|TestMakeChangelogCheck|TestRepositoryFragmentsValid|TestFold|TestMakeChangelog' ./internal/changelog/
go run ./cmd/changelog --check; echo "exit=$?"
make check
```

**Assumptions already checked**
- `--check` cannot collide with a version: `versionToken` regex at `fold.go:16`.
- No test asserts the usage string: `grep -rn "usage: changelog" .` finds only `cmd/changelog/main.go:12`.
- Current fragments are valid: read with `cat changes/unreleased/*.md`.
- New files are absent: checked with `ls`.

**Reopen the plan instead of widening the change if**
- making `Check` work would require changing `fragment` or `Fold` behavior or error text;
- making CI enforce the check would require editing `.github/workflows/**` or `.swarm/validation/**`;
- a current fragment on the updated base fails the check (fix the fragment in a separate change, not here).

**What this change breaks**
- `cmd/changelog/main.go:12` usage string: updated. No test asserts it (grep above).
- `Makefile` `check` target: `make check` also runs `changelog-check`. `README.md:81` ("same formatting, vet, staticcheck, and race-enabled tests as CI"): preserved unchanged. It is still accurate, because CI enforces the same rule through the repository-level test.
- `AGENTS.md:69` (`make check`): protected, preserved unchanged.
- `TestMakeChangelog`, `TestFold*`, `TestRepositoryUnreleasedEmpty`: preserved unchanged and must still pass.
- `docs/developer.md:611-625`: one sentence added, existing text preserved.

## Operator guidance

> Refresh the existing narrowly scoped check-only changelog plan onto current approved main including the shared executable test helper. Preserve fragment format/fold output, no protected policy edits: wire cmd/changelog --check, make check and a repository-level test into existing CI. Read-only pinned directory validation reports all malformed fragments; missing and empty directories pass. Avoid unrelated changes.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# TEST_PLAN — ISSUE-179

All new tests go in `internal/changelog/check_test.go` and reuse the `put`/`read`/`fixture` helpers from `fold_test.go` and the shared `internal/testutil.WriteExecutable` helper.

## AC1 — `go run ./cmd/changelog --check` exits non-zero naming each malformed file and reason, writes nothing, exits zero for missing or empty dirs, covered by tests including a two-bullet fragment

| Test | Setup | Expectation |
|---|---|---|
| `TestCheck/missing` | fixture without `changes/` | `Check` returns nil |
| `TestCheck/empty` | empty `changes/unreleased/` | nil |
| `TestCheck/non-md only` | `keep.txt` only | nil |
| `TestCheck/valid` | `01.md` = `- One`, `02.md` = `- Two\n  more` | nil |
| `TestCheck/two-bullet` | `78.md` = `- One\n- Two` | error contains `78.md` and `each fragment holds exactly one bullet` |
| `TestCheck/reports all` | `01.md` valid, `02.md` = `- a\n- b`, `03.md` = `paragraph`, `04.md` = `` | error names `02.md`, `03.md`, `04.md`, not `01.md`; each has its own reason line, in filename order |
| `TestCheck/directory .md` | `dir.md/` directory | error names `dir.md` |
| `TestCheck/symlink .md` | `link.md` → outside file (skip if symlinks are unsupported) | error names `link.md`; outside file unchanged |
| `TestCheck/fifo .md` | `pipe.md` FIFO (skip without `mkfifo`) | returns promptly with an error naming `pipe.md`; FIFO still exists |
| `TestCheck/unsafe dir` | `changes/unreleased` is a symlink to a directory | non-nil error |
| no writes (every case) | snapshot of the tree (relative path → mode, size, modtime, content) before and after `Check`, failures included | snapshots equal; `CHANGELOG.md` and all fragments byte-identical |
| `TestMakeChangelogCheck` | build `cmd/changelog`, copy `Makefile` into the fixture, `go` wrapper written with `testutil.WriteExecutable` running `"$3"` | `make changelog-check GO=wrapper` exits 0 with no fragments and with valid fragments; after adding a two-bullet `bad.md`, exits non-zero with output containing `bad.md` and the reason; tree snapshot unchanged |
| CLI exit codes (manual) | repository root | `go run ./cmd/changelog --check; echo $?` → `0`. In a temp copy with a two-bullet fragment → non-zero, stderr names the file |

Command: `go test -race -run 'TestCheck|TestMakeChangelogCheck' ./internal/changelog/`

## AC2 — make check (or a required check) runs the fragment check so a malformed fragment fails validation

- `Makefile`: `check: lint race changelog-check`. Verify with `make -n check | grep 'changelog --check'`.
- `TestRepositoryFragmentsValid`: `Check(filepath.Join("..", ".."))` must return nil. It runs under the existing required `test` check (`go test ./...`) and the CI `go test -race ./...` step without any protected-file edits, so a PR that adds a malformed fragment fails both `make check` and CI.
- Negative demonstration (manual, then reverted): `printf -- '- a\n- b\n' > changes/unreleased/zz-bad.md; make changelog-check; go test -run TestRepositoryFragmentsValid ./internal/changelog/` → both fail and name `zz-bad.md`; `rm changes/unreleased/zz-bad.md`.

## AC3 — make check passes

- `make check` exits 0. This covers gofmt, vet, staticcheck, race tests, and changelog-check.
- Required policy checks run directly: `gofmt -s -l .` (empty), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, `go test ./...`.

## Regression (out-of-scope behavior preserved)

- The existing `TestFold*`, `TestMakeChangelog`, `TestFragmentBranchesMerge`, and `TestRepositoryUnreleasedEmpty` pass unchanged. This shows the fragment format and the fold output did not change.
- `changes/unreleased/179.md` passes `Check` (covered by `TestRepositoryFragmentsValid`).

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Refresh the existing narrowly scoped check-only changelog plan onto current approved main including the shared executable test helper. Preserve fragment format/fold output, no protected policy edits: wire cmd/changelog --check, make check and a repository-level test into existing CI. Read-only pinned directory validation reports all malformed fragments; missing and empty directories pass. Avoid unrelated changes.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

VERDICT: APPROVED

| Requirement | Audit |
|---|---|
| Report every malformed fragment | Sorted `.md` names, existing `fragment` parser, and `errors.Join` preserve each filename and reason rather than stopping early. Tests cover two bullets and multiple simultaneous failures. |
| Missing/empty directories succeed | `Sub(create=false)` handles `os.ErrNotExist`; empty and non-Markdown-only directories produce no errors. Explicit tests cover these cases. |
| Root-bound reads reject unsafe entries | Verified `safefs.Sub`, `OpenDirectory`, and `ReadFile` in `internal/safefs/root.go`: pinned directory traversal rejects symlink components, and regular-file validation rejects directories, symlinks, and FIFOs before reading. Planned tests exercise these boundaries. |
| No writes or fold-output changes | Design uses read-only APIs, reuses `fragment`, and leaves `Fold` unchanged. Tree snapshots cover success and failure; existing fold and make regression tests remain intact. |
| PR validation catches bad fragments | Verified `.github/workflows/swarm-validate.yml` runs `go test -race -timeout 15m ./...` on pull requests. Proposed `TestRepositoryFragmentsValid` checks the actual repository fragments within that suite and the existing required `go test ./...` check. `make check` also gains a direct check prerequisite. Negative verification exercises both paths. |
| Protected policy and scope | No protected edits are planned. The WorkUnit expressly permits wiring through `make check`; policy/template additions are identified as follow-up work rather than blocking implementation. Required fragment and concise developer documentation are included. |
| Test helper convention | Verified `TestMakeChangelog` uses `testutil.WriteExecutable`; the new make test explicitly preserves this helper and its executable-wrapper argument convention. |
| Required validation | TEST_PLAN maps all three acceptance criteria to tests or reproducible commands, including `make check` and the compiled required checks. |

No blocking findings. Read PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md, and REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md independently against the WorkUnit and source. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md contains repeated design/test-plan evidence; it supplies no separate approval authority.

Implementation notes: close every opened root/directory descriptor; snapshot unsafe entries with metadata/link-aware handling so the verification itself neither follows symlinks nor reads FIFOs. These are routine details of the approved read-only design.

This is plan approval; the proposed implementation and checks have not yet been executed.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Independently review the refreshed read-only changelog check plan against exact criteria. Verify all malformed fragments reported, missing/empty directories succeed, root-bound reads reject unsafe filesystem entries, no writes/fold-output changes, and actual PR CI catches bad fragments via existing checks without protected policy edits. Preserve test helper convention. Write only REVIEW.md and optional LESSONS.md.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
